title: United's Miles Were Worth More Than United #shorts
summary: In June 2020 United valued MileagePlus at about $22 billion, almost double its $11.7 billion market value.
sources: Delta Air Lines 2025 Form 10-K (Item 1): "In 2025, remuneration from American Express totaled $8.2 billion, which we expect to grow to $10 billion over the next few years"; "Our most significant and valuable contract to sell miles relates to our co-brand credit card relationship with American Express"; "In 2025, 12% of revenue miles flown on Delta were from award travel ... approximately 35 million award tickets"; fuel cost $9,819 million: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/27904/000002790426000013/dal-20251231.htm

Delta December quarter and full year 2025 results (Jan 13, 2026): operating revenue $63.4 billion, operating income $5.8 billion (9.2% margin), pre-tax income $6.2 billion: https://news.delta.com/delta-air-lines-announces-december-quarter-and-full-year-2025-financial-results

Delta's $9.0 billion of financings secured by the SkyMiles program, September 2020 (Kilpatrick Townsend release): https://ktslaw.com/insights/news/news-release/2020/9/kilpatrick-townsend-advises-delta-air-lines-on-9-billion-skymiles-financings
Our calculation: $8.2B American Express remuneration / $9.819B fuel = 84%. Remuneration is revenue, not profit; it is compared with operating income only to show its size.
United's $6.8 billion financing secured by MileagePlus (July 7, 2020): https://www.kirkland.com/news/press-release/2020/07/kirkland-reps-ua-on--financing-mileageplus

United valued MileagePlus at about $22 billion, almost double its $11.7 billion market capitalization; 71% of MileagePlus cash flow in 2019 from third parties (Bloomberg, via Executive Traveller, June 2020): https://www.executivetraveller.com/news/how-united-airlines-took-a-7bn-mortgage-on-its-frequent-flyer-scheme

scenes.narration: In {2020,|twenty twenty,} United said its frequent flyer program was worth about {$22 billion.|twenty-two billion dollars.}
The whole airline was worth {$11.7 billion|eleven point seven billion} on the stock market.
Most of that miles money came from credit card partners, not from flying.
The miles were worth more than the planes.
